pois.name: Chrysler Museum of Art
pois.intro: The Chrysler Museum of Art is an art museum on the border between downtown and the Ghent district of Norfolk, Virginia. The museum was founded in 1933 as the Norfolk Museum of Arts and Sciences.

pois.name: USS Wisconsin BB-64
pois.intro: USS Wisconsin is an Iowa-class battleship built for the United States Navy in the 1940s and is currently a museum ship. Completed in 1944, the ship was assigned to the Pacific Theater during World War II, where she participated in the Philippines campaign and the Battles of Iwo Jima and Okinawa.

pois.name: F/A-18
pois.intro: The McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft. Designed by McDonnell Douglas and Northrop, the F/A-18 was derived from the YF-17 that lost against the YF-16 in the United States Air Force's lightweight fighter program.

pois.name: USS Norfolk Bell
pois.intro: The second USS Norfolk was the first destroyer leader of the United States Navy. Originally projected as a hunter-killer cruiser, she was in service until 1970, and was scrapped in 1974.

pois.name: Portsmouth Lightship Museum
pois.intro: United States Lightship 101, known as Portsmouth as a museum ship, was first stationed at Cape Charles, Virginia. Today she is at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard Museum in Portsmouth, Virginia.

pois.name: Children's Museum of Virginia
pois.intro: The Children's Museum of Virginia is the largest children's museum in the state of Virginia. It is located in Olde Town Portsmouth at 221 High Street.

pois.name: The MacArthur Memorial Museum
pois.intro: The MacArthur Memorial is a memorial, museum, and research center about the life of General Douglas MacArthur. It consists of three buildings on MacArthur Square in Norfolk, Virginia.

pois.name: Virginia Zoological Park
pois.intro: The Virginia Zoological Park, commonly known as the Virginia Zoo, is a 53-acre zoo located adjacent to Lafayette Park in Norfolk, Virginia, United States. The zoo opened in 1900, and was accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums in 1987.

pois.name: Portsmouth Colored Community Library Museum
pois.intro: Portsmouth Community Library, also known as the Portsmouth Colored Community Library, is a historic library building located at Portsmouth, Virginia. It was built in 1945 at 804 South Street.

pois.name: Saint Pauls Catholic Church
pois.intro: St. Paul's Catholic Church is a historic Roman Catholic church located in Portsmouth, Virginia, United States.

pois.name: Commodore Theatre
pois.intro: Commodore Theatre is an historic movie theater located at Portsmouth, Virginia. It was built in 1945 in the Streamline Art Deco style, and originally sat 1,000 people.

pois.name: Owen B. Pickett U.S. Custom House
pois.description: Designed to resemble a Roman Temple. Except for about one year during the Civil War, this building has served as the U.S. Custom House since it opened in 1858.

pois.name: Gatehouse

MacArthur Center
pois.intro: MacArthur Center was a shopping mall in Norfolk, Virginia, United States, in the center of the Hampton Roads metropolitan area. Built by Taubman Centers, the mall is owned by the City of Norfolk since August 2023.

pois.name: Town Point Park
pois.intro: Town Point Park is a 7-acre waterfront city park on the Elizabeth River in Norfolk, Virginia, USA. The park hosts major outdoor concerts, award-winning festivals and special events each year to include Norfolk Harborfest, Bayou Boogaloo, and 4 July Celebrations. Norfolk Festevents programs Town Point Park on behalf of the City of Norfolk.

pois.name: Seaboard Coastline Building
pois.intro: Seaboard Coastline Building, also known as Old City Hall, is a historic train station located at Portsmouth, Virginia. The original section was built in 1894-1895 by the Seaboard Air Line Railroad.
